citation.authors: Erukainure OL, Oyebode OA, Sokhela MK, Koorbanally NA et al

cited_by.title: Kola nut: caffeine, the heart and health claims

record.population: Laboratory models (cell-free assays and rat liver tissue)
record.design: In vitro and ex vivo study of a caffeine-rich Cola nitida infusion
record.finding: The concentrated infusion was 80.08% caffeine by HPLC, scavenged free radicals and inhibited carbohydrate-digesting enzymes (alpha-glucosidase and alpha-amylase) in the lab. The authors suggest antioxidative and antidiabetic properties, with caffeine the major constituent.
record.note: A concentrated infusion in the lab, not a nut; the 80% caffeine is for the concentrate and says nothing about caffeine per nut.
